title: Sunlight and Starlight
subject: Science
source: NYSED 2026 Grade 5 ELS Released Items, Questions 1-4
directions: Base your answers to questions 1 through 4 on the information below and on your knowledge of science.

intro.html: Our solar system exists in the Milky Way Galaxy. There are about 100 billion stars in the Milky Way and the Sun is one of them. The Sun is the only star in our solar system. The Sun is responsible for many patterns and events that occur on Earth.

constellations.html: After the Sun sets, some stars are visible in the night sky. The model below shows different groups of stars (constellations) that are visible in the night sky in Rochester, New York as Earth orbits the Sun.

constellations.caption: Model of Constellations
constellations.alt: The Sun is at the center of an oval orbit labeled Earth’s actual positions in orbit. Dots on the orbit mark Earth’s position on the 21st of each month: Sept 21 at the top, then Aug 21, July 21, June 21 at the right side, May 21, Apr 21, Mar 21 at the bottom, Feb 21, Jan 21, Dec 21 at the left side, Nov 21, and Oct 21. Twelve constellations, drawn as stars connected by lines, surround the orbit: Aries, Pisces, and Aquarius above the top of the orbit; Capricornus and Sagittarius to the right; Scorpius at the lower right; Libra and Virgo below the bottom of the orbit; Leo and Cancer at the lower left; Gemini and Taurus at the upper left.
